newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian ironworks losses deepen in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian ironworks losses deepen in 1996.

text.p: Slovenia's ironworks Slovenske Zelezarne posted deeper losses in 1996 of 7.3 billion tolars ($46.6 million) from 4.6 billion in 1995, the Ministry of Economic Activities said on Friday.
"Losses increased due to expensive loans and the strong tolar, which is hampering the competitiveness of ironworks abroad," Branka Kostic, state secretary of industry at the ministry, told Reuters.
A change in accounting standards was also partly to blame for the larger losses, she said.
Sales fell to 52.1 billion tolars from 54.2 billion.
Zelezarne, currently state-owned, would likely be privatised by the end of next year, she said.

"A law on the privatisation of the company is expected to be prepared in the next two weeks. Privatisation could be completed by the end of 1998," Kostic added. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
